minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved goat hikes on town land and an Eagle Scout kiosk; firearms ban left for the 17 Feb hearing.
minutes.summary: The commission approved an Eagle Scout kiosk at Proctor Park, commercial goat hikes on conservation land, a septic replacement and several certificates, and ratified an enforcement order. Most of the meeting was a line-by-line review of the draft land use regulations, including firearms, bow hunting, dogs and enforcement. Firearms and bow hunting were left for the public hearing.

A member offered to help with materials costs; the scout is fundraising himself.
The goat operators charge a fee for hikes to offset the cost of keeping the goats.

decisions.decision: Goat hikes approved subject to proof of insurance, police notification and the agent's check that the use is allowed.
Draft regulations to go to public hearing on the 17th. The commission rejected the attorney's edits to the definition wording.
Straw poll on firearms deferred until the member who was absent can take part, after the public hearing.
Bow hunting left as written in the draft for the hearing; counsel's reply on Hunting Hill is awaited.
Agent to add a police-notified box to the form and send it before the 17th.
Agent to have the Spring Street owners file an RDA for the plantings.
Forestry cutting plan for Hollis Road to come to the first March meeting.

what_happened.line: The commission approved commercial goat hikes on conservation land, with proof of insurance and police notice required within a week.
It approved an Eagle Scout kiosk project at Proctor Park by a 5-0 roll call vote.
Most of the meeting went to a line-by-line review of the draft land use regulations; the commission sent them to a public hearing on the 17th.
Firearms and bow hunting were left for the hearing, and a firearms straw poll was deferred until an absent member can take part.
The commission extended the Hickory Hills Lake order of conditions one year past the end of the emergency declaration, 4-2 as captioned.

why_it_matters: The draft land use regulations, including rules on firearms, bow hunting and dogs on town conservation land, are not settled and will be argued at a public hearing where residents can comment.
Goat hikes are a new commercial use of town conservation land, so the insurance and police-notice conditions are the terms that govern it.
watch_next: Public hearing on the draft land use regulations on 17 February, with the 203 Fire Road 16 and 36 Cushing Lane hearings also continued to that date.
Counsel's reply on bow hunting at Hunting Hill, and the firearms straw poll after the hearing.
